summary: A 1936 Aermotor tower with a 7-foot metal cab on the Fort Apache reservation; the register says it is still active, and a 2016 looting probe went to the BIA.

facts.design: Aermotor tower with a 7-by-7-foot metal cab

access.note: On the Fort Apache Indian Reservation (tribal land); the register gives no public visiting information.

events.note: 123-foot Aermotor tower with a 7-by-7-foot metal cab, per the register
October 2016 investigation into reported vandalism and looting; Bureau of Indian Affairs to decide further action

evidence.supports: built 1936 as a 123-foot Aermotor tower with 7x7 metal cab
evidence.quote: Aermotor tower with 7’x 7’ metal cab was built in 1936

evidence.supports: register calls it the tallest fire tower in Arizona
evidence.quote: is the tallest fire tower in Arizona

evidence.supports: still active; base for a helitack fire crew

evidence.supports: on the Fort Apache reservation, Navajo County
evidence.quote: Fort Apache White Mountain Indian Reservation

evidence.supports: administered by the White Mountain Apache Agency

notes_for_editor: Height is the register's 123 ft; not converted because the register does not say whether that is to the cab floor. 'Tallest fire tower in Arizona' is the register's own claim, unverified. The 'still active' statement is from the register page, which gives no date for it, so staffing is left out of facts. Access 'restricted' is an editorial call for tribal land, not a source term. The 2016 vandalism outcome was not found. The 1989 SW Region report has no Limestone entry (grep found none). Counties are spelled Navajo (register, FFLA) and Navaho (West Lookouts). The register's 'Fort Apache-White Mountain' spelling is in its Location field. Record coordinates match the register exactly; the FFLA list is about 0.0003 degrees away.
